stem:
Irfan lists the main gases in air: nitrogen, oxygen, argon, carbon dioxide, and water vapour. These gases are not chemically combined into one substance.

Which claims are correct? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: Air is a mixture because several gases are present together without forming one new substance.
The gases in air keep their own properties and are not chemically combined.
Air is a compound because several gases are listed together.
Air is pure oxygen because living beings need oxygen.

teacher.key_rationale: Air has several gases that are not chemically combined, so it is a mixture. Listing gases does not make a compound, and needing oxygen does not make air pure oxygen.
